what_it_does: Quantum computers work by running pulses of microwave energy at qubits (the quantum equivalents of classical bits), and converting a high-level quantum circuit (a sequence of logical gates) into those physical pulses is called pulse generation. Today's pulse generation methods are either slow to compute or produce pulses that take a long time to execute because they do not expose enough opportunities to run operations in parallel. EPOC attacks this by first simplifying the circuit using a mathematical shorthand called ZX-Calculus, which strips away unnecessary operations and reveals equivalent but more compact representations. The circuit is then split into independent segments that can be compiled in parallel, and each segment is synthesized into pulses at a finer grain than current tools allow, reducing both compile time and the total duration of the resulting pulse sequence.
